title: Chuchvara (small Uzbek boiled dumplings in broth)

ingredients.name: sour cream or yogurt, and vinegar, to serve

steps: Knead the flour, egg, water and salt into a stiff dough and rest it for 30 minutes.
Mix the meat, onion, pepper and a little salt into a smooth filling.
Roll the dough out very thinly and cut it into squares of about 4 cm.
Put a small amount of filling on each square, fold diagonally to make a triangle and press the edges firmly, then pull the two corners together and pinch them to make a little ear shape.
Bring the stock to a gentle boil, add the dumplings and cook for 7 to 10 minutes until they float and are tender.
Serve in bowls with the broth, herbs, a spoonful of sour cream or yogurt and a few drops of vinegar.

title: Dimlama (Uzbek layered meat and vegetable stew)

ingredients.name: lamb, cut into large pieces (with some fat)
small head of white cabbage, cut into wedges
bell peppers, cut into thick slices

steps: Layer half of the onion rings in the bottom of a heavy pot with a tight lid, then put the lamb on top and season it with salt and pepper.
Add the remaining vegetables in layers without stirring, in this order: potatoes, carrots, cabbage, peppers and tomatoes, seasoning each layer lightly with salt.
Tuck the garlic cloves and half of the herbs in among the vegetables. Add no water, or at most a few spoonfuls.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for about 1.5 to 2 hours, without lifting the lid, until the meat is tender; the vegetables cook in their own steam and juices.
Scatter the rest of the herbs on top and serve the dimlama in layers, scooping down to the bottom so every portion gets meat and vegetables.

title: Manti (Uzbek steamed lamb and onion dumplings)

ingredients.name: lamb tail fat or butter, finely diced
butter, to grease the steamer; plain yogurt to serve

steps: Knead the flour, water and salt into a firm dough, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the lamb, onions, fat, cumin, pepper and salt well so the onions release their juice.
Roll the dough out thinly and cut it into 10 cm squares.
Place a heaped spoonful of filling in the centre of each square and pinch the opposite corners together to make closed parcels.
Grease the steamer tiers well and set the manti in with a little room around each.
Steam over rapidly boiling water for 40 to 45 minutes until the dough looks glossy and the filling is cooked through.
Serve hot with plain yogurt, black pepper and a little melted butter.

title: Mastava (Uzbek rice and vegetable soup with lamb)

ingredients.name: lamb or beef, cut into small cubes
salt, black pepper, fresh dill and cilantro, and plain yogurt to serve

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the meat, then add the onion and carrots and fry for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes and pepper and cook until they soften, about 5 minutes.
Add the water, salt and pepper, bring to a boil and simmer, covered, for 40 minutes until the meat is tender.
Add the potatoes and the rice and simmer for another 20 minutes until both are soft and the soup has thickened slightly.
Serve hot, topped with chopped herbs and a spoonful of yogurt.

title: Norin (Uzbek hand-cut noodles with boiled meat)

ingredients.name: beef or lamb on the bone

steps: Simmer the meat with the whole onion and a pinch of salt in the water for about 2 hours until it is tender and falling off the bone.
Mix the flour, egg, water and a pinch of salt into a stiff dough, knead it smooth and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll the dough out very thin and cut it into long thin noodles.
Lift out the meat, shred or slice it thinly, and strain the broth.
Boil the noodles in salted water until tender, 3 to 4 minutes, then drain.
Fry the sliced onion in a little oil or fat from the broth until soft, add a ladle of broth and simmer briefly.
Mix the noodles and meat on a platter, scatter the onions over them, season with plenty of pepper and herbs, and serve with a bowl of hot broth.

title: Obi non (Uzbek round tandoor-style bread)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and sugar in a bowl, add the warm water and knead for 10 minutes into a smooth, elastic dough. Cover and let it rise for 1 hour.
Divide into 2 balls, flatten each into a round about 2 cm thick with a slightly thinner centre and a fat rim.
Press a pattern into the centre with a docking tool or a fork so it does not puff, then brush with beaten egg and scatter with the seeds.
Preheat the oven to its highest setting (about 250 C / 480 F) with a baking stone or heavy tray inside.
Bake the loaves on the hot stone or tray for 12 to 15 minutes until deeply golden and the crust is crisp.
Cool slightly and tear into pieces at the table.

title: Oshi toki (Uzbek stuffed grape leaves)

ingredients.name: grape leaves, fresh or brined and rinsed
salt and black pepper to taste; yogurt to serve

steps: Blanch fresh leaves in hot water for 1 minute (or soak and rinse brined leaves) and trim off the stems.
Fry the onions in the oil until soft, let them cool, then mix them with the meat, rice, herbs, cumin, salt and pepper.
Place a leaf shiny-side down, put a spoonful of filling at the stem end, fold in the sides and roll up tightly into a small cylinder.
Line a pot with a few leaves and pack the rolls in tight layers.
Pour in the hot water or stock, weigh the rolls down with a plate and cover. Simmer gently for about 45 minutes until the rice and meat are cooked.
Serve hot or warm with a bowl of plain yogurt.

title: Qovurdoq (Uzbek fried meat and potatoes)

ingredients.name: lamb, cut into small cubes (with some fat)
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Heat the oil in a deep heavy pan until hot and brown the lamb on all sides, about 10 minutes.
Add the onions and carrots and fry for 8 to 10 minutes until golden and soft.
Add the potatoes, cumin, salt and pepper, stir, and cover. Cook on medium-low heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potatoes are cooked through and browned in places.
Stir in the herbs and serve hot from the pan with flatbread and a salad of sliced tomatoes and onions.

title: Samarkand non (thick Samarkand-style bread)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt and add the warm water. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and let it rise, covered, for about 1.5 hours.
Divide the dough into 3 or 4 pieces and shape each into a thick, round, high-sided loaf with a small dip in the centre.
Stamp or dock the centre of each loaf densely with a fork.
Whisk the egg yolk with 1 tablespoon of water and brush it over the loaves, then sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake on a preheated stone or tray at 240 C (465 F) for 18 to 20 minutes until golden brown, with a dense, chewy crumb and a crisp base.
Cool on a rack and serve fresh.

title: Shurpa (Uzbek lamb and vegetable soup)

ingredients.name: lamb on the bone (ribs, shank or shoulder), in large pieces

steps: Put the lamb in a large pot with the cold water, bring to a boil and skim off the foam carefully.
Add the onion and a little salt, cover and simmer for 1 hour until the meat is almost tender.
Add the carrots and cook for 15 minutes, then add the potatoes, tomatoes, peppers and quartered onion in large pieces.
Season with coriander, black pepper and more salt, and simmer for another 30 minutes until everything is soft but still holding its shape.
Serve in deep bowls with a piece of meat and generous chunks of vegetable in each, topped with fresh herbs, with flatbread alongside.

title: Somsa (Uzbek baked lamb and onion pastries)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder or leg, cut into very small cubes
lamb tail fat or butter, diced

steps: Knead the flour, water and salt into a firm dough, then roll it into a thin rectangle, spread with the softened butter, roll it up like a log and chill for 30 minutes.
Mix the lamb, onions, fat, cumin, pepper and 1 tsp salt for the filling. The onions should be plentiful for juiciness.
Cut the dough log into 12 slices and roll each into a thin round.
Place a generous spoonful of filling in the middle of each, fold the edges over to form a square or triangle and pinch the seams closed.
Set the somsas seam-side down on a lined tray, brush with egg yolk and scatter with seeds.
Bake at 200 C (400 F) for 15 minutes, then reduce to 180 C (350 F) and bake for about 25 more minutes until deeply golden. Serve hot.

title: Uzbek lagman (pulled noodles with lamb and vegetables)

ingredients.name: fresh or dried wheat noodles (thick spaghetti works)
small daikon radish or turnip, cut into thin strips (optional)
salt, black pepper and cilantro, to taste

steps: Heat the oil in a wide pot and fry the lamb over high heat until deeply browned.
Add the onions, cook until golden, then add the carrots, radish and peppers and cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and tomatoes and cook for 5 more minutes until the tomatoes have broken down.
Pour in the stock, season, cover and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes until the meat is tender and the sauce is thick but spoonable.
Boil the noodles in plenty of salted water until just cooked, then drain.
Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle the lamb and vegetable sauce over them and sprinkle with cilantro and black pepper.

title: Uzbek plov (lamb, carrot and rice pilaf)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder or leg, cut into large chunks
long-grain or pilaf rice, rinsed until the water runs clear
yellow carrots (or ordinary carrots), cut into thick matchsticks
large onions, sliced into half rings
vegetable or cottonseed oil (or 100 ml oil and 50 g lamb fat)
garlic, whole, papery outer layers removed
ground cumin, plus 1 tsp whole cumin seeds

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot or deep cast-iron pan until it is shimmering and almost smoking, then brown the lamb well on all sides, about 8 minutes.
Add the onions and fry for 10 minutes until deep golden brown.
Add the carrots, spread them evenly and cook, stirring, for about 8 minutes until they soften. Add the cumin, barberries and salt, then pour in about 250 ml of hot water.
Lower the heat, cover and simmer for 40 minutes. This slow-cooked base is called the zirvak.
Sprinkle the drained rice evenly over the top without stirring. Press the whole garlic head into the middle.
Pour the remaining hot water gently over the back of a spoon so it comes about 2 cm above the rice. Cook uncovered on high heat until the water has been absorbed.
Gather the rice into a mound, poke several holes down to the base with a spoon handle, cover tightly and steam over the lowest heat for 20 to 25 minutes.
Turn the plov over gently to mix the meat and carrots through the rice, and serve on a large platter topped with the garlic.

title: Uzbek shashlik (lamb skewers with onions)

ingredients.name: lamb leg or shoulder, cut into 3 cm cubes
lamb fat or tail fat, cut into small cubes (optional)
large onions, 1 sliced into rings and 1 sliced thinly for serving

steps: Toss the lamb with the onion rings, salt, cumin, pepper and vinegar, cover and marinate in the fridge for 3 to 4 hours.
Thread the lamb on metal skewers, alternating a cube of fat after every three cubes of meat if you are using it.
Prepare a hot charcoal grill or heat a grill pan and cook the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Serve right off the skewers with raw sliced onions, tomato and flatbread.
